title: Affine Artin--Rees stabilization of coherent formal kernel images
statement:
theorem coherentFormalModule_kernel_affine_bound {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (F H : CoherentFormalModule X I) (α : F ⟶ H)
    (U : X.affineOpens) :
    ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ (l m : ℕ) (h : m + c ≤ l) (W : X.Opens), W ≤ U.1 →
      Set.range ((Abelian.image.ι (kernel.ι (α.hom.app (op l)) ≫
        F.obj.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_trans (Nat.le_add_right m c) h)).op)).app W) =
      Set.range ((Abelian.image.ι (kernel.ι (α.hom.app (op (m + c))) ≫
        F.obj.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_add_right m c)).op)).app W)

source.place: Lemma 087X, proof of claim (a): affine localization and Artin--Rees calculation

proof.text: Restrict the formal systems and morphism to the affine open U. Restriction preserves coherence, annihilation and the defining quotient-transition isomorphisms. Identify U with Spec of its section ring and use the affine formal-module equivalence to obtain finite modules M,N over its adic completion and a linear map f, with level n equal to reduction modulo I^(n+1).

The completion is Noetherian. Apply Artin--Rees to im(f) inside N: choose c such that I^r N intersect im(f) equals I^(r-c)(I^c N intersect im(f)) for r >= c. Lift the summands through f to obtain f inverse(I^r N) = ker(f) + I^(r-c) f inverse(I^c N).

Put r=l+1. If l >= m+c, then r-c >= m+1, so the second summand vanishes modulo I^(m+1) M. The image of the reduced kernel in level m is exactly the image of ker(f), independent of l, and in particular equal to its value at l=m+c. The same calculation covers c=0 and the zero and unit ideals.

Kernels and images of maps of quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent. The affine module/sheaf correspondence and ideal-product comparison identify the two image subsheaves over U. Equality of monic subsheaves identifies the ranges of their section maps on every subopen W of U, not only on affine subopens.
